# Minecraft Fabric 1.21.11 — Friends Modpack

Pick one tier. All three ship the same mods and shaders (Iris + Complementary
Unbound); they differ in shader profile, render distance, and RAM.

| Tier | For | Shader profile | RAM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dalit | very low end / integrated graphics | POTATO | 3G |
| Pandit | mid range | MEDIUM | 5G |
| Modi | dedicated GPU | HIGH | 8G |

Re-running your one-liner is also the update path.

## Dalit

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A1K2S3/minecraft/main/client/install.ps1))) -dalit
```

## Pandit

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A1K2S3/minecraft/main/client/install.ps1))) -pandit
```

## Modi

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A1K2S3/minecraft/main/client/install.ps1))) -modi
```

## Linux / macOS

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/A1K2S3/minecraft/main/client/install.sh | sh -s -- --dalit
```
# Server

Fabric 1.21.11 on [`itzg/minecraft-server`](https://github.com/itzg/docker-minecraft-server).
The mod list is **not** written here — it is generated into `mods.generated.env` from
`../mods.json` by `../scripts/generate`.

## Layout

| File                 | Committed           | What it is                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docker-compose.yml` | yes                 | The server and the lazymc proxy that sleeps/wakes it, exactly as they run. Contains no secrets.                              |
| `bootstrap`          | yes                 | Restore the world from Backblaze B2 if this machine has none, then start. Run this first on a fresh machine.                 |
| `restart`            | yes                 | Save the world, recreate the containers, report. The deploy step.                                                            |
| `.env.example`       | yes                 | Template for `.env`.                                                                                                         |
| `.env`               | **no** — gitignored | `RCON_PASSWORD`, `PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY`, plus the four Backblaze B2 values `bootstrap` restores from. This repo is public; the real values live only here and on the VM. |
| `mods.generated.env` | yes                 | `MODRINTH_PROJECTS=...`, generated. Never hand-edit.                                                                         |
| `data/`              | no — gitignored     | World, logs, and the mods the container downloads.                                                                           |
| `.restore-stage/`    | no — gitignored     | Scratch space `bootstrap` downloads a snapshot into. Deleted on exit.                                                        |

`docker-compose.yml` pulls both env files:

```yaml
env_file:
  - ./.env
  - ./mods.generated.env
```

so `RCON_PASSWORD` is only ever the `${RCON_PASSWORD}` reference in the compose file, and
the mod list is only ever the generated file.

## First run on a fresh VM

```sh
git clone https://github.com/A1K2S3/minecraft.git /root/mc-repo
cd /root/mc-repo/server
cp .env.example .env
$EDITOR .env          # RCON_PASSWORD, PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY + the four Backblaze B2 values
./bootstrap --logs
```

**Use `bootstrap`, not `docker compose up -d`, the first time.** It asks the B2
repository named in `.env` whether a world is already backed up there. If one is, it
downloads it into `data/` _before_ the server starts, so the container boots the real
world. If the repository is empty — a genuinely new server — it just starts and the world
generates.

**Automatic backups are currently disabled** (see Backups below), so B2 holds only the
last snapshot taken before they were switched off. Anything played since then exists
only in this VM's `data/`.

`bootstrap` is safe to re-run. Once `data/world` exists it never touches it again, so it
also works as the everyday "start the stack" command.

If it cannot read the repository — wrong key, wrong `RESTIC_PASSWORD`, B2 unreachable —
it **refuses to start** rather than generating a fresh world on top of a perfectly good
backup. Fix `.env` and re-run.

The container downloads every mod in `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` on boot, plus their required
dependencies (`MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES: required`). First boot takes a few minutes.
Because of lazymc (below), that first boot happens when the first player joins.

## Sleeping when empty

Players reach the server through a **playit.gg** tunnel (the `playit` container; the
tunnel and its public address are configured in the playit.gg dashboard, pointing at
`127.0.0.1:25565`). That lands on **lazymc** on port 25565, never on `mc` directly
([`lazymc-docker-proxy`](https://github.com/joesturge/lazymc-docker-proxy)). It starts the
`mc` container when someone joins and `docker stop`s it once nobody has been online for
10 minutes (`lazymc.time.sleep_after`), so the JVM exits and its 8G of RAM is freed.

- **Joining a sleeping server** wakes it. The client is held, then shown a "server is
  starting" message if boot takes longer; reconnect after a minute or two.
- **While asleep** the server list still answers, with a sleeping MOTD.
- **Nothing ticks while asleep.** Farms, ComputerCraft turtles and chunk loaders stop
  with the server. A turtle mid-program reboots when the server next starts.
- `mc` has `restart: "no"` on purpose — lazymc owns its lifecycle. `lazymc` itself has
  `restart: unless-stopped`, so after a VM reboot the proxy is back and `mc` stays asleep
  until someone joins.
- On startup lazymc stops `mc` if it is running, so right after `restart` or `bootstrap`
  `mc` shows as exited. That is expected.
- Both containers sit on `mc-net` with static addresses (`172.29.0.2` / `.3`) because
  lazymc must reach `mc` while it is stopped and has no DNS name.
- lazymc mounts the Docker socket to start and stop `mc`. That is root-equivalent on the
  host; the container is the published upstream image.

To force the server up without joining: `docker compose start mc`.

## Deploying a mod change

From your machine:

```sh
$EDITOR mods.json          # add, remove, or re-pin a mod
scripts/generate
git add mods.json server/mods.generated.env client/mods.generated.tsv client/purge.generated.txt
git commit -m "Add <mod>"
git push
```

On the VM:

```sh
cd /root/mc-repo
git pull
./server/restart          # flush the world, recreate the containers, report
```

`server/restart` is the safe way to do the last step: it broadcasts a warning to anyone
online, forces a `save-all flush` over RCON so no progress is lost, then runs
`compose down` + `compose up -d` so the new `mods.generated.env` takes effect. Add
`--logs` to follow the server log afterwards. It refuses to run if `.env` is missing, and
refuses to stop an online server whose save could not be confirmed unless you pass
`--force`. Running it twice is safe.

The manual equivalent is `docker compose up -d` from this directory — compose recreates
the container when an env file changes, so a `git pull` followed by `up -d` is the whole
deploy. `restart` just adds the save and the guards. Nothing else on the VM needs editing — in
particular, never edit `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` by hand on the server, because the next
`git pull` would overwrite it and the client would silently drift out of sync.

Removing a mod from `mods.json` stops the container downloading it, but does not delete
the jar already sitting in `data/mods/`. Delete it there too, then restart.

## Server-only vs shared mods

`side` in `mods.json` decides this and nothing else does. A mod marked `server` never
reaches a friend's client, and the client installers actively remove server-only jars
from `mods/` (their filename prefixes are generated into `client/purge.generated.txt`).
A mod marked `both` must be present on both sides at the same version or clients will be
rejected at login.

## Common operations

```sh
./bootstrap                          # restore-if-needed, then start (fresh machine, or just start)
./restart                            # save the world, recreate, report (see above)
./restart --logs                     # same, then follow the log
docker compose ps -a                 # is it up (mc "exited" = asleep)
docker compose logs -f mc            # tail the server log
docker compose logs -f lazymc        # sleep / wake events
docker compose start mc              # wake the server without joining
docker compose exec mc rcon-cli      # console; reads RCON_PASSWORD from the env
```

## Backups

**Automatic backups are currently disabled.** The `itzg/mc-backup` sidecar that pushed
the world to Backblaze B2 nightly has been removed from `docker-compose.yml`, to be
reimplemented later. Until then the world exists only in this VM's `data/`.

The last snapshot it took is still in the B2 restic repository, and `bootstrap` can still
restore it — so keep the four B2 values in `.env`, and never lose `RESTIC_PASSWORD`: it
is the only key to that snapshot.

To see what is in B2:

```sh
docker run --rm --env-file "$(pwd)/.env" restic/restic:latest snapshots
```

### Restore

On a new machine, or after losing `data/`, that is just the fresh-VM flow above —
`bootstrap` restores automatically when no local world is present.

To deliberately roll the current world back to the B2 snapshot (the last one taken before
backups were disabled):

```sh
docker compose down          # bootstrap refuses to overwrite a running server
./bootstrap --force-restore  # deletes data/world, restores the snapshot, starts
```

`--force-restore` is destructive and says so before acting. Without it, `bootstrap`
never touches an existing world.
# Sleep when empty: players connect to lazymc, not to mc. lazymc starts the mc
# container when someone joins and stops it (docker stop, so a clean save) once
# nobody has been online for lazymc.time.sleep_after seconds -- the JVM exits
# and its RAM is freed. While mc is down, lazymc answers the server list itself
# and holds a joining client until the server is up.
services:
  lazymc:
    image: ghcr.io/joesturge/lazymc-docker-proxy:latest
    container_name: lazymc
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      # lazymc reads server.properties from here. Read-only.
      - ./data:/server:ro
      # How it starts and stops the mc container. This is root on the host --
      # the price of an on-demand server.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    networks:
      mc-net:
        ipv4_address: 172.29.0.2
    # Docker keeps container logs forever by default; cap them so they cannot fill
    # the disk.
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"

  # Public entry point: the playit.gg agent tunnels players in to lazymc on the
  # host's 25565. The tunnel itself (and its public address) is set up in the
  # playit.gg dashboard, pointing at 127.0.0.1:25565.
  playit:
    image: ghcr.io/playit-cloud/playit-agent:1.0
    container_name: playit
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      SECRET_KEY: "${PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY}"
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"

  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    container_name: mc
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    # No published port: all traffic goes through lazymc.
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    # lazymc owns this container's lifecycle. Any restart policy would bring it
    # straight back up every time lazymc puts it to sleep.
    restart: "no"
    # lazymc stops the server with `docker stop`. The image turns SIGTERM into a
    # clean `stop` and allows it 60s (STOP_DURATION); Docker's default 10s grace
    # would SIGKILL it mid-save.
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    # A static address so lazymc can reach mc while mc is stopped and has no DNS
    # entry. It must match lazymc.server.address below.
    networks:
      mc-net:
        ipv4_address: 172.29.0.3
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: "10m"
        max-file: "3"
    labels:
      - lazymc.enabled=true
      - lazymc.group=mc
      - lazymc.server.address=172.29.0.3:25565
      # Sleep 10 minutes after the last player leaves, so a quick reconnect
      # does not pay for a cold boot.
      - lazymc.time.sleep_after=600
      # A cold boot of this modpack (longer on a deploy, which re-downloads
      # mods) can outlast lazymc's 300s default.
      - lazymc.server.start_timeout=600
      # What the server list shows while mc is asleep. Protocol 774 is 1.21.11;
      # without these the list reports a version mismatch.
      - lazymc.public.version=1.21.11
      - lazymc.public.protocol=774
    # ./.env             -- secrets, NOT committed (see .env.example)
    # ./mods.generated.env -- MODRINTH_PROJECTS, generated from ../mods.json by scripts/generate
    env_file:
      - ./.env
      - ./mods.generated.env
    environment:
      EULA: "true"
      TYPE: "FABRIC"
      VERSION: "1.21.11"
      MEMORY: "8G"
      DIFFICULTY: "normal"
      MODE: "survival"
      ONLINE_MODE: "false"
      MAX_TICK_TIME: "-1"
      VIEW_DISTANCE: "6"
      SIMULATION_DISTANCE: "5"
      USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
      ENABLE_RCON: "true"
      # ":offline" makes the image derive each op's offline-mode UUID locally
      # instead of looking the name up on Playerdb/Mojang. With ONLINE_MODE false
      # that is the UUID players actually join with, and the lookup fails outright
      # for names with no Mojang account (Sid19s), which aborts startup.
      # Add new ops the same way: Name:offline.
      OPS: "Guardian:offline,Chaukidaar:offline,Sid19s:offline"
      OP_PERMISSION_LEVEL: "4"
      RCON_PASSWORD: "${RCON_PASSWORD}"
      MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES: "required"
      MODRINTH_PROJECTS_DEFAULT_VERSION_TYPE: "beta"

networks:
  # Outside Docker's default 172.17.0.0/16 so the static addresses above stay
  # stable across container restarts.
  mc-net:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.29.0.0/24
# Generated by scripts/generate from mods.json. Do NOT hand-edit.
MODRINTH_PROJECTS=spark,fabric-api,lithium,ferrite-core,balm,forge-config-api-port,polymer,midnightlib,puzzles-lib,universal-graves,repurposed-structures-fabric,fallingtree,jei:27.23.0.71,saturated-eating,waystones:21.11.9+fabric-1.21.11,travelersbackpack:1.21.11-10.11.10,biomes-o-plenty:21.11.0.32,terrablender:21.11.0.0,glitchcore:21.11.0.4,storagedrawers:1.21.11-20.0.0,carry-on:2.9.2,farmers-delight-refabricated:1.21.11-3.6.13,adorn:7.6.1-fabric,modern-decorations-mod:26.7.0,fantastic-wings:21.11.1,datapack:towers-of-the-wild-reworked:Pr8Jhst4,create-fly:1.21.11-6.0.9-5,cc-tweaked:1.117.1,expanded-weaponry,animal_feeding_trough,connectiblechains,c2me-fabric,lithostitched,terralith,datapack:towns-and-towers,architectury-api,cloth-config,enderite-mod:1.8.2,grind-enchantments,skinrestorer,eunomia:fab-mc-1.21.11-0.3.14,zannaghs-armor-hider:fab-mc-1.21.11-0.14.4,create-ultimate-factory:2.2.4
# Copy to server/.env and fill in the real values. server/.env is gitignored and
# must never be committed -- this repo is public.
#
#   cp .env.example .env && ${EDITOR:-nano} .env
#
# RCON password for the running server. Any long random string; rotate it by
# editing .env and running `docker compose up -d`.
RCON_PASSWORD=changeme

# playit.gg agent secret key (players connect through the playit.gg tunnel). Get it
# from the playit.gg dashboard when adding the agent. Treat it like a password.
PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY=

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backblaze B2 restic repository holding the last world snapshot. Automatic
# backups are currently disabled (server/README.md, "Backups"); these values are
# used only by ./bootstrap to restore that snapshot, and it refuses to run
# without them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The restic repository, on B2's S3-compatible endpoint. Take the endpoint from
# your bucket's page in the B2 console (it looks like
# s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com -- the region digits differ per account) and
# keep the s3:https:// prefix and the bucket name:
#
#   RESTIC_REPOSITORY=s3:https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com/my-mc-backups
#
# restic also has a native b2: backend, but both restic's and Backblaze's docs
# recommend the S3 API instead, so use the s3: form above.
RESTIC_REPOSITORY=

# Encryption password for the restic repository.
#
# READ THIS: restic encrypts the repository with this password. There is no
# reset and no recovery -- lose it and the B2 copy of the world is permanently
# unreadable, even though the bytes are still sitting in the bucket. Keep a
# copy somewhere that is NOT this VM (a password manager). Pick any long random
# string the first time; it is then fixed for the life of the repository.
RESTIC_PASSWORD=

# B2 application key, scoped to the backup bucket only (create it in the B2
# console under Application Keys). restic speaks S3 to B2, which is why these
# carry AWS names:
#   keyID          -> AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
#   applicationKey -> AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
# Restoring needs read on the bucket; the (currently disabled) backups also
# need write.
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=

Author: Adarsh Senghani <adarshco077@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Oct 22 20:40:53 2026 +0530

    Fix AbstractMethodError on remapped mod-interface methods (hot air burner crash)
    
    BlockEntityLiftingGasProvider, BlockEntityPropeller and BlockEntitySubLevelReactionWheel
    declared abstract getLevel()/getBlockPos()/getBlockState() and relied on Minecraft's
    BlockEntity to implement them. Loom renames the Minecraft methods to intermediary
    (method_10997/method_11016/method_11010) in release jars but leaves the interface
    methods alone, so the hot air burner, steam vent, propellers, propeller bearings,
    encased fans and flywheels threw AbstractMethodError on client and server ticks.
    
    - aeronautics: rename to aeronautics$getLevel/aeronautics$getBlockPos, implemented
      explicitly in HotAirBurnerBlockEntity and SteamVentBlockEntity; update call sites.
    - sable: sable$getLevel/sable$getBlockPos/sable$getBlockState as defaults that cast to
      BlockEntity (remapped call); update call sites.
    - e2e: required RemapSafetyTest (RemapSafety) fails on any abstract mod-interface method
      that is unimplemented at runtime or only implemented by a Minecraft method; also run
      at start-up. Required burner/steam vent tick test in AeronauticsHotAirTest.
    - PORTING.md: rule against relying on Minecraft names for mod-interface methods.
    - Bump sable to 2.0.6+mc1.21.11-port.1 and aeronautics to 1.3.2+mc1.21.11-port.1.

content.text:
I reproduced it. The cause is a bug in our first Aeronautics release (v2026.10.18), and the 10.22 release fixes it.

## What crashed
I rebuilt your server on my machine with the same 43 mods from your `mods.generated.env`, plus the exact Aeronautics jars the server ran (I checked their checksums). Then I placed a hot air burner under an envelope dome and gave it a redstone signal. The server died on the next balloon tick:

```
Description: Ticking block entity
java.lang.AbstractMethodError: Receiver class ...HotAirBurnerBlockEntity does not define or inherit
an implementation of the resolved method 'abstract net.minecraft.class_1937 getLevel()'
of interface ...BlockEntityLiftingGasProvider
  at BlockEntityLiftingGasProvider.tryJoinBalloon(BlockEntityLiftingGasProvider.java:101)
  at BlockEntityLiftingGasProvider.tickBalloonLogic(...:225)
  at HotAirBurnerBlockEntity.lazyTick(...:113)
```

## Why
- **The bug:** the burner's balloon code asks a mod interface for `getLevel()` and expects Minecraft's block entity to answer under that name.
- **Why it passed our tests:** in the development build Minecraft's method is also called `getLevel()`, so it matches.
- **Why it broke on your server:** in a release jar, Minecraft's methods carry their release names (`getLevel()` is `method_10997`). The build tool renames our calls to Minecraft methods, but it leaves our own interface's method names alone. So on a real server the interface's `getLevel()` has nothing behind it.
- **When it fires:** nothing breaks until the burner gets a redstone signal. That's the moment it tries to find or create a balloon.
- **Why the whole server went down:** Minecraft treats any error while ticking a block entity as a fatal crash. While that burner stayed powered, the server would crash again each time it loaded that chunk.

All our tests ran on the development build, so none of them could see this. The Lithium crash before it was the same kind of problem: it only showed up on a real server.

## Fixed in 10.22
A teammate's commit `1c5c20c` ("hot air burner crash") renames the interface methods so they no longer clash with Minecraft names. The same commit also fixes steam vents, propellers, propeller bearings, encased fans and flywheels on ships, and adds a check for this kind of bug. On the same modpack with 10.22:
- The powered burner ran with no crash.
- A balloon ship rose from y −54 to y −13 in 30 seconds, while an unpowered control ship fell to the ground.

## Things to check
- **Which version crashed:** the server switched to 10.22 on 10-22 at 20:51 and Aeronautics was removed on 10-23. If your crash was before the VM pulled the 10.22 commit and restarted, this is it. To be sure, look at `server/data/crash-reports/` on the VM. If the report doesn't show this `AbstractMethodError`, send it to me, because then it's a different bug.
- **Re-adding Aeronautics is safe on 10.22.** Every player needs the matching `...-port.1` jars, so they should re-run the installer.
- **Your local `integration` branch is behind:** the fix is only on `origin/main`.

I added a line about this to `PROGRESS.md` but haven't committed it. The test servers and crash report are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-akshatkhair-Documents-Projects-minecraft-create-fly/ad4c3c4a-4eb3-4a3d-9d40-870fbc35734f/scratchpad/`.
can your confirm now all the aeronautics related things would work fine ?

I'll check this properly on release builds rather than guess. content.text:
I can confirm 10.22 has no more crashes like the balloon one, and everything I could run on a server worked. I can't promise "everything" will work, because I couldn't test the game client or real players.

## What I checked (10.22, with your server's full modpack)

**1. Code scan of every class (client and server).** I wrote a checker that reads all 2,648 classes in the three jars, using the names Minecraft has in a release build. It looks for exactly the kind of bug that crashed your server: a method that exists in testing but is missing in a real install.
- **10.18:** it finds 7 broken block entities: the burner, steam vent, both propeller bearings, and the wooden, andesite and smart propellers. Your balloon was one of these.
- **10.22:** it finds zero, client side included.
- The only leftovers are optional hooks into Explorer's Compass, Nature's Compass and ModMenu. They only load if those mods are installed, and you don't have them.

**2. Real server, 43 mods plus Aeronautics 10.22.**
- **All 48 blocks:** I placed every Aeronautics and Simulated block, each on a running motor with a redstone signal, and left them ticking. No errors.
- **A real airship:** burner balloon, steam vent, all three small propellers on motors, both propeller bearings, levitite, steering wheel, throttle, all the sensors, magnet, portable engine, winch, swivel bearing and potato cannon. I assembled it and it climbed to about y 160, where it levelled off.
- **Restart:** saved, stopped, restarted. The ship reloaded in the air where it was. No errors.

## What I couldn't test
- **The game client:** rendering, shaders, block menus, and flying a ship as a player. The code scan covers the crash type that hit you, but not visual or gameplay bugs.
- **Right-click blocks:** the physics assembler only assembles when a player right-clicks it, so I assembled ships with a command instead.
- **Multiplayer and long sessions:** several players, lag, big ships over hours.

## Before re-adding it
- **Retired prefixes:** remove `sable-fabric-`, `simulated-fabric-` and `aeronautics-fabric-` from `retired_prefixes` in `mods.json`. Until you do, `scripts/generate` will refuse to build, so you can't ship a half-broken setup by accident.
- **Server memory:** the server is set to 8 GB but the VM only has about 7.2 GB, and it's already swapping. Physics ships add memory load, so that could cause crashes or lag that have nothing to do with these bugs. Lowering it to around 5–6 GB is safer.
- **First flight:** after friends re-run the installer, fly one ship together for a few minutes. That's the quickest way to cover the client side.

I logged the results in `PROGRESS.md` (not committed yet).

content.text:
It's the real server world, and it has Sable `sublevels/` folders, so ships saved while Aeronautics was installed may still be in there. That makes it good test material.

## Yes, test on your client, but fix first
Your crash report already shows how the client test will end today: the game crashes as soon as a heated balloon is drawn. So I'd fix the bug before you play:

1. **Fix the renderer.** `ClientBalloonEffectRenderer` writes each balloon's settings while its draw step is still open. Writing them all first, then drawing, should fix it. It's a small change.
2. **Check it in our test client.** I'd add a balloon scene to `tools/e2e.sh` and run it with and without Sodium. That first tells us whether the crash needs shaders at all or happens on every client; I suspect every client, but haven't confirmed it. Iris isn't in our test setup, so step 3 covers that.
3. **Then the real check on your Minecraft:**
   - **Separate profile:** use a separate TLauncher profile and game folder (a copy of your mods and config plus the fixed jars), so your normal install for the friends' server isn't touched.
   - **A copy of the world:** extract the backup into scratch and run it as a local server with the full server modpack I already have set up, then join from your client. This matches the real server/client setup better than single-player, and it shows whether the saved ships still load. The original archive stays untouched as the backup.
   - **What to try:** with Iris on (it was on when you crashed) and off: build and light a balloon, fly it, use the propellers, right-click the physics assembler, use the steering wheel, leave and rejoin, and restart the server. I'll watch the logs while you play.

## Things to know
- **Memory:** the server needs about 4 GB and the client with shaders 5–8 GB, on 16 GB total. Close other heavy apps.
- **Disk:** extracting the world adds about 5 GB.
- **The archive is inside the git repo.** `world/` is 5.1 GB, untracked and not ignored, so a careless `git add .` would try to commit it. I'd move it out or add it to `.git/info/exclude`.

Should I start with steps 1 and 2 (fix the renderer and confirm it in the test client), then set up the separate profile and world copy for you to play?
ya do these and run my minecraft and test on it without shaders

4. Start a local server on a copy of your world, launch your Minecraft into it, build and light balloons there, and watch the logs and screenshots.

assert "inheritsFrom" not in v, "expected a flattened version json"
def allowed(rules):
    if not rules: return True
    ok = False
    for r in rules:
        osr = r.get("os", {})
        match = (not osr.get("name") or osr["name"] == "osx") and not r.get("features")
        if match: ok = r["action"] == "allow"
    return ok
cp, missing = [], []
for lib in v["libraries"]:
    if not allowed(lib.get("rules")): continue
    parts = lib["name"].split(":")
    if len(parts) == 4 and parts[3] != "natives-macos-arm64": continue
    g, a, ver = parts[:3]
    jar = f"{a}-{ver}" + (f"-{parts[3]}" if len(parts) == 4 else "") + ".jar"
    p = f"{MC}/libraries/{g.replace('.', '/')}/{a}/{ver}/{jar}"
    (cp if os.path.exists(p) else missing).append(p)

if missing: print("MISSING", *missing, file=sys.stderr)
game, name, server = sys.argv[1:4]

content.text:
I found a second crash, fixed it, and tested the fix on your Minecraft without shaders. Your balloon now works.

## The second crash
Your crash report from Oct 22, 22:01 was on 10.22, the version with the first fix. 10.22 still crashed the **game client** as soon as a lit balloon came into view. The code that draws the hot-air effect inside the envelope prepared its data in the wrong order: it wrote to graphics memory while a drawing step was still open, and Minecraft 1.21.11 throws an error when that happens. Shaders don't matter: I got the same crash on plain Minecraft and on Sodium without Iris. Our tests missed it because their test ship had a burner with no envelope above it, so a balloon never formed.

## The fix
- **Code:** the balloon renderer now prepares everything before it starts drawing. The changes are in `ClientBalloonEffectRenderer` and `HeatedCulledRenderRegion`.
- **Test:** the flight test scene now builds a lit balloon. It crashed before the fix and passes after, on both plain Minecraft and Sodium.
- **New jar:** `aeronautics-fabric-1.21.11-1.3.2+mc1.21.11-port.2.jar`. My code scan on it comes back clean.
- **Pushed** as branch `fix/balloon-render-pass` (commit `20d66c8`). I haven't merged it into main or made a release.

## Test on your Minecraft
I launched your TLauncher install, the same mods you play with plus the fixed jars, from a separate game folder with Iris shaders off. It joined a local server running a copy of your server world. As player `Tester` it:
1. Built and lit a balloon on your terrain; the balloon filled and rendered.
2. Turned it into a ship, which flew up to about y 186 and levelled off.
3. Saw the server restart: the client disconnected cleanly, and the ship reloaded in mid-air.

content.text:
I haven't confirmed that everything about flying works yet. So far your Minecraft has rendered a heated balloon without crashing and a test ship has flown. Driving a ship yourself with propellers, throttles and the wheel is what we're about to test.

The mini ship is built on the water next to your friend's ship, and you're standing on its deck:
- **Deck:** 9 × 5 planks.
- **Lift:** a propeller bearing with a 3 × 3 sail rotor, run through a throttle.
- **Forward:** a stern wooden propeller, run through its own throttle.
- **Steering:** a steering wheel at the bow, wired through a gearbox to a sideways propeller.

What I've checked so far, before launch:
- **Throttles:** both control their rotors. You moved them earlier (they went from 15 to 1 and 5) and the rotor speeds followed, from 0 up to 224 and 160 RPM. They're closed again now, so the ship will float first.
- **Steering:** the wheel and side propeller are idle. That's normal until someone holds the wheel, so your first turn is the real test.

**Next step is yours:** hold right-click on the Physics Assembler in front of you. I'm watching the server and will report the ship's position and speed once it assembles. Then try the lift throttle, the forward throttle and the wheel.

A few things to know:
- **Your friend's big ship isn't flying.** It's still ordinary blocks. I added a plank deck, four rotors and glue on top of it, all on this test copy only. You switched to the mini ship before it could be assembled. I found two limits along the way:
  - The `/sable assemble connected` command counts water as part of the ship, so it can't lift a ship that sits in the sea. The in-game Physics Assembler doesn't have this problem.
  - The Physics Assembler only uses honey glue whose centre is within 48 blocks of it, so a very long ship needs several glue patches.
- **A Create deployer couldn't right-click the assembler, or even a lever, on this server.** I didn't dig into why.
- **Nothing here touches your real world.** It's all on the scratch copy. Your real install and the world archive haven't been changed.

content.text:
I found what happened, from the blocks left behind and the dropped items:

1. **Launch worked.** You assembled the mini ship at 15:10:04. It floated at the waterline (y 63.3, mass 34), and none of the rotors were spinning yet.
2. **It moved and tipped.** In about 40 seconds it travelled roughly 7 blocks toward the stern corner of your friend's ship. It also turned about 90° and rolled, sinking a little (y 60.2, falling at 2 blocks/s). That fits a top-heavy design: a single plank layer with the motor, transmission, bearing and sail rotor stacked three blocks high in the middle.
3. **Then it came apart, at 15:10:46.** The ship stopped being a physics ship. Its sail rotor was put back as normal blocks at (117–119, 63, 10–12), right against your friend's hull. Most other parts (throttles, motors, wheel and so on) are floating around as **dropped items**; they all dropped at the same moment. That's what a Physics Assembler disassembly does when the ship is tilted and overlapping other blocks: anything that can't be placed back on the grid drops as an item. My guess is the assembler got right-clicked a second time. Did you click it again, or break something?
4. **The steering propeller never left.** It's still at its build spot (126, 63, 19), so it wasn't part of the ship. Steering wouldn't have worked on this build.
5. **Nothing crashed.** Neither the game nor the server had an error through the whole ride.

What I'd change for a second mini ship:
- **Stability:** a 2-layer hull that's wider than it is tall, with the lift rotor sitting low.
- **Space:** build it in open water well away from your friend's ship.
- **Side propeller:** fix it so it's actually attached to the ship.
- **Seat:** add a seat by the wheel, so you're carried along steadily while steering.

I built the new mini ship on the water where you were hovering. You're standing on its deck next to the Physics Assembler. All the parts placed cleanly, both motors drive their transmissions, and the throttles are closed, so it will just float until you push them.

**How to fly it.** The bow points east, toward the steering wheel; the stern is west, where the rear propeller is.

1. **Launch:** hold right-click on the Physics Assembler in front of you, **once**. It should settle and float. Clicking it again later turns the ship back into blocks. That's probably what broke the last one apart.
2. **Sit:** use the seat behind the steering wheel.
3. **Up and down:** use the **lift throttle** on the deck, under the sail rotor on its stern side. Hold right-click and push it to rise, ease it back to hover or sink. The rotor is strong, so go slowly; hover is a little past halfway.
4. **Forward:** use the **forward throttle** by the rear propeller. I reversed its motor because the last ship went backwards. If it still goes backwards, tell me and I'll flip it.
5. **Steering:** hold right-click on the **steering wheel** and turn it to swing the bow left or right. Let go to stop turning.
6. **Landing:** bring the lift throttle down slowly onto the water. Then click the assembler to turn the ship back into blocks.

Compared with the last one: it has a two-layer hull, the lift motor and transmission are built into the hull so the rotor sits lower, there's a seat, and the glue has extra room around every part.

I'm watching the server for the launch. When it happens I'll tell you whether every part came along, especially the side propeller that does the steering, which got left behind last time.

content.text:
The cockpit is done, and the board is readable from the seat (in your screenshot: **LEFT LEVER = LIFT**, **WHEEL = STEER**, **RIGHT LEVER = FORWARD**).

**Your cockpit,** sitting in the seat facing the board and wheel:

| Where | Control | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| In front of you | **Steering wheel** | Hold right-click and turn left or right to swing the ship's nose that way. Let go to go straight. |
| On your left post | **Lift lever** | Push to rise, pull back to sink. Half pushed gives about half power. |
| On your right post | **Forward lever** | Push to go forward, pull back to stop. |
| Just behind you, left side | **Physics Assembler** | Click once to launch, once more after landing to turn the ship back into blocks. |
| Sign board, above and around the wheel | **Instructions** | Top row: what each control does. Bottom row: start and land steps (partly behind the wheel). |

**To fly:**
1. Right-click the **Physics Assembler** once. The ship becomes a physics ship and floats on the water.
2. Sit in the **seat**.
3. Push the **left lever** a little at a time until it rises, then ease it back toward the middle to hold height. The rotor is strong, so go slowly.
4. Push the **right lever** to go forward.
5. Hold the **wheel** and turn to steer.
6. To land, bring the left lever back slowly so it settles on the water, then click the assembler.

I tested both levers before launch: the left lever spins the lift rotor (half gives 112 RPM, closed gives 0), and the right lever spins the rear propeller (open gives 256). The steering and the forward direction can only be tested once you're flying. If forward pushes you backwards, or the wheel doesn't turn the ship, tell me and I'll fix it.

Two notes:
- **Levers start fully pulled back (off).** That's why nothing moves until you push them.
- **The lift rotor already picked up its sails** while I was testing, so it shows up as a separate spinning part. That's normal; the last ship took its rotor along the same way.

I'm still watching the server and will tell you once the ship launches and whether everything came along.

content.text:
The crash was in the server, not your game, and it's a real bug in our port that would also have hit your friends' server. I fixed it, rebuilt the flying boat, and restarted your game onto its deck.

**Why it crashed:** the Physics Assembler couldn't turn the tilted ship back into blocks. The code meant to show you a "couldn't align" message instead used a text helper that only exists in the game client. A server can't load client-only code, so the whole server went down. On your friends' server, anyone landing a tilted ship would have taken the server down the same way.

**The fix:**
- **Server text:** that message, and four other server-side messages with the same problem, now build their text without the client-only helper.
- **Wider check:** I scanned every server-side class in the three mods for other calls into client-only code and found nothing else that would run on a server.
- **Pushed:** the new Simulated jar (`…-port.1`) is installed on the test server and your test client, and the fix is pushed to branch `fix/balloon-render-pass` (commit `1976a65`).

**The new boat:** same mini design as before, and checked before you joined:
- **Lift:** the lift motor runs the right way now. Half lift spins the rotor at −112, the direction that lifted our test ship; the broken one was +112.
- **Levers:** both start pulled fully back (off) and are on wireless links beside the seat.
- **Sign board:** at the front explains each control.

**How to fly:**
1. Right-click the **Physics Assembler** once. It's just behind you, on your left.
2. Sit in the **seat**, facing the wheel and board.
3. Push the **left lever** slowly until you rise. Ease it back toward the middle to hover.
4. Push the **right lever** to go forward.
5. Hold the **wheel** and turn to steer.
6. To land, bring the left lever back slowly. Only click the assembler when the boat is **level and resting on the water**; if it's tilted it refuses now instead of crashing.

Nothing has been tested in flight yet: forward and steering only show once you're up. If the right lever moves you backwards or the wheel doesn't turn the boat, tell me. I'm watching the boat's height and speed once you launch.
if needed remove the older things which we tried

I'll clean up the test world, leaving only the new boat. What goes:
1. The **balloon test ship** still floating at y 186.
2. Everything I added to **your friend's ship**: the plank deck on top, the four rotors and their spinning sails, the assemblers, all the glue. It goes back to exactly how they built it.
3. **Leftovers from the first mini ship**: stray sails and the side propeller, plus dropped items.
4. The **force-loaded chunks** I turned on.

Your usage limit has been reached, so I have to stop here. I haven't built the new non-flipping boat yet.

**What's done:**
- **Three real crashes found and fixed, all pushed** to branch `fix/balloon-render-pass`:
  - The balloon burner crashed the server in 10.18 (already fixed in 10.22).
  - Seeing a lit balloon crashed the game client.
  - Landing a tilted ship crashed the server.
- **Old test builds removed:** the balloon test ship, everything I'd added to your friend's ship (it's back to how they built it), and the first mini ship's leftovers. Your world's own force-loaded chunks were cleared by my cleanup and then restored.
- **Flip v3 and test ship A removed.** Test ship B (twin rotors) is still sitting on the ground at about (90, 66, 30), since it dropped when its rotors failed to start.
- **Notes:** added the findings to `PROGRESS.md`, not committed.

**What I learned about the flipping:**
- **It isn't width alone.** v3 had a gyro bearing, a 7-wide hull and a stone keel, and it still flipped once you pushed the lift.
- **The boats were underpowered.** One 3×3 rotor at full power (1,382 thrust) barely beats the weight of a 7-wide hull (about 110 × gravity 11 ≈ 1,215). You have to push the lever hard, and that's when they tip.
- **With too little lift it doesn't flip.** It just sits in the water, leaning about 8°.

**What's left:**
1. **Testing method:** my mid-air tests didn't work. After `/sable assemble area` the rotors never start, and I can't move the levers on a flying ship by command, because its blocks live in Sable's own plot files rather than the normal world. That needs solving before I can prove a design doesn't flip without you at the controls.
2. **New boat by you:** with that sorted, build the new version where you are. It would have two counter-rotating gyro rotors with bigger sails, which is your idea and the most likely fix, and enough lift to rise at about half lever.
3. **Your friends' server:** release the fixed jars there (`aeronautics port.2`, `simulated port.1`), once you decide.

content.text:
I can't read your assembled ship's blocks directly yet: Sable keeps them in its own plot storage format, and decoding that takes a while. But the save already answers the main question. Your world has **"Head in the Clouds"** unlocked. The game only awards that once a balloon actually forms over a burner and fills with hot air. So **the balloon code is working**: no crash, no error in the log, the burner finds the envelope and fills it. Most likely it just isn't making enough lift for the weight it's carrying.

**How lift works in this mod:**
- **Lift:** each cubic metre of hot air lifts **1.5** units of mass.
- **Burner output:** one burner puts out at most **500 m³**, and only with a **full-strength redstone signal (15)** and its hot-air setting scrolled to the maximum (500). With a weaker signal or a lower setting it puts out proportionally less.
- **Balloon size:** a balloon holds no more hot air than the space inside the envelope. A 5×5×4 inside space holds 100 m³, which lifts only 150, however many burners you add.
- **Ship weight:** planks and logs weigh 0.5 each, most other blocks (stone, machines, ores) 1.0, envelope blocks 0.25.
- **Example:** a 9×5 plank deck with two layers is about 45 already. Add envelope, machinery and gear and you quickly need hundreds of m³ of hot air.
- **Fill time:** a balloon fills gradually, taking roughly 10–20 seconds to get near full. Your game is also lagging (`Can't keep up! 78 ticks behind`), which slows that further.

**Things to check, roughly in order:**
1. **Goggles on the burner:** wear the Aviator's Goggles (you have the recipe) and look at the burner. It shows the balloon's volume, how full it is, and how much it can lift. Compare that number with your ship's weight.
2. **Redstone:** the burner needs a full-strength signal (lever or redstone block, 15). A long redstone line or analog source gives less hot air.
3. **Hot-air setting:** scroll on the burner's value box and turn it up to 500.
4. **Bigger balloon:** if lift is below the ship's weight, make the envelope bigger (taller and wider inside) and add burners, about one burner per 500 m³ of inside space.
5. **Clear line upward:** nothing solid should sit between the burner and the envelope ceiling, or the burner won't find the balloon.
6. **Fully closed envelope:** the sides need to be sealed; only the bottom can be open.

If you'd like a definite answer instead of a checklist, tell me roughly how big the balloon is (inside size), how many burners there are, and what powers them, or put the goggles on and tell me the numbers. I can also write a reader for Sable's plot storage and list your ship's exact blocks and weight. That takes longer, but then I can tell you exactly how much balloon you need.

Separately, the boat-stability tests I was running before this found what makes the propeller boats flip: they need a **gyroscopic** propeller bearing **exactly over the centre of the hull**. I was about to build a balanced version for you.

Both repos are pushed. I skipped the final in-game test you stopped. Instead I booted a dedicated server with the full new pack (all 166 mods, including the 6 new jars) and it started with no errors. I haven't run the gameplay sweep or a client test on these exact jars.

**The mod:** release **v2026.10.25** is up on the mod's GitHub, built from `main` (`1976a65`). It contains:
- **Aeronautics `port.2`:** fixes the game crashing when a lit balloon is in view.
- **Simulated `port.1`:** fixes the server crashing when a tilted ship can't be turned back into blocks.
- **Sable `port.1`:** unchanged.

**Your friends' modpack repo** (`A1K2S3/minecraft`, commit `64c3894`):
- **Aeronautics is back:** Aeronautics, Sable and Create Simulated are pinned to the new release.
- **Your three mods are added,** each pinned to one version for both server and clients:
  - **Weapons Expanded** 1.9.3.1.
  - **Enchantments Expansion** v1.2.0. I used its Fabric mod version, which fits the repo better than the datapack zip.
  - **Extended Vanilla Endgame** 1.0.0.
- **Repo script:** the mod list generator can download mods from a GitHub release again, and it still removes modflared from friends' installs.

**To roll it out:**
1. On the VM: `git pull`, then `./server/restart`.
2. Every friend re-runs their installer one-liner. It picks up the new jars and replaces the old Aeronautics ones.

**Still open:**
- **Shaders:** a lit balloon with Iris shaders turned on hasn't been tested.
- **Server memory:** the VM is set to 8 GB but has only about 7.2 GB, and this update adds more mods. I'd lower the server memory to 5–6 GB before restarting.
- **Building flying boats:** use a **gyroscopic propeller bearing**, placed **exactly over the middle of the hull**. In my tests that stayed within 5° of level; anything off-centre, or a normal bearing, flipped. The test scene that showed this is still uncommitted in my scratch copy.
- **Your local `integration` branch** is behind `main`. I didn't touch it.
- **PROGRESS.md:** updated but not committed.

That error was my fault: the link I gave you is served as a generic file (`application/octet-stream`), and SkinRestorer only accepts links served as images. This one works:

```
/skin set web slim "https://s.namemc.com/i/eca1f9a3e434107b.png"
```

It's the same skin, identical pixel for pixel; it's just stored in a more compact PNG format. A server can download it and gets it back as `image/png`, which is what SkinRestorer checks for. Use it the same way as before: as Guardian on your friends' server, or in any world that has SkinRestorer.
